headline: An AI test that estimates a woman's five-year breast cancer risk from her mammogram can now be bought online across the United States for $249.
score_reason: Launch dates from 1 Oct 2026 and STAT's piece is a paywalled follow-up; lowered by 1 from 5.
importance_line: Women with a recent mammogram can now pay out of pocket for an AI risk score, but an outside surgeon warns that FDA authorization shows safety rather than better outcomes and a high-risk result can cause anxiety and extra scans.
summary: Everyday Health reports that Clairity Breast, an FDA-authorized AI tool that estimates breast cancer risk over the next five years from a screening mammogram, is now sold across the US through the digital health company Everlywell for $249, not covered by insurance, after launching only in parts of Massachusetts and Colorado. STAT, in its series on what clinical AI costs patients, reports that the maker, Clairity, went straight to patients because waiting for doctors and insurers would have taken too long.
notes: STAT+ original (https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/why-clairity-took-breast-cancer-risk-prediction-ai-directly-to-patients/) is paywalled; only its opening lines and subhead were readable. Product facts come from Everyday Health (6 Oct 2026).
